basics.name: Matt Ji
basics.label: Systems & Infrastructure Engineer
basics.summary: Engineer and risk analyst, ten years where operations meets software. I build the systems other people depend on: a thirteen-host NixOS fleet declared once and rebuilt from the commit, Go services with an append-only event log, and an email archive that classifies its own mail. Before that, four years of asset management for a solar portfolio above $100M, and research on heliostat metrology at Fraunhofer ISE. Operations, to me, means measure, change, verify — with the way back designed in.

work.name: Bountystash
highlights: Held the configuration of thirteen hosts in one declaration: the wanted state lives in the repository, every machine pulls it from there, and nothing is hand-edited on the target.
Ran every change through a gate that executes in CI and on the host; anything done by hand twice became a check instead of a habit.
Treated a release as one step — build, gate, activate — with rollback as a pointer to the previous generation rather than a restore procedure.
Measured service health instead of decorating it: a sentinel writes job status, generation age, disk pressure and PSI into a ledger every fifteen minutes and pages on any state that is not ok.
Kept capacity as a budget: disk, memory and closure size carried numbers and a check, so growth was visible before a full disk made it urgent.
Collected logs and events from the fleet through journald and an event store, and traced faults by host, unit and time window.
Administered Linux below the application: systemd units with per-slice memory limits, cgroups, nftables default-deny, and DNS or MTU faults diagnosed with tcpdump instead of a ticket.
Issued access through an in-house certificate authority with short-lived certificates; secrets are encrypted per host with SOPS and age.
Built Go and Python services behind one task interface, so a repeated operation is a command with a check rather than a runbook someone remembers.
Developed an options and hedging algorithm for weather derivatives.
Advised clients and acted as internal risk manager for a large German energy trader.
Built an immutable web templating language that is immune to script injection.
Steered gas storage and gas swing trading models as risk manager for EWE Trading.
Reviewed bug bounty programmes.

projects.name: nixconfig
projects.description: One flake declares thirteen NixOS hosts, an SSH certificate authority, SOPS-encrypted secrets and a taskfile as the operator interface. CI runs the same module gate the machines run.

projects.name: bountystash
projects.description: A Go service that turns a request into an immutable, content-addressed specification. Append-only events, a terminal UI and curl endpoints ship in one binary.

projects.name: Risk Calculation Engine (Swirl Engine)
projects.description: Green's theorem on stochastic polygons: a Go fuzzer generates shapes, a Nushell and Awk pipeline drives the computation, and a Nix development environment pins the tools.
highlights: Designed a swirl engine on Green's theorem to compute polygon areas from random geometric data.
Implemented a shape fuzzer in Go that generates stochastic polygons to load the engine.
Orchestrated the pipeline in Nushell and Awk, sidestepping compiler limits for compute-heavy mathematics.
Containerised the environment with Nix Flakes for reproducible Go 1.16+ development.

projects.name: fibtransponder
projects.description: A Fibonacci-radix state machine that processes a bit stream with bounded work per step. A corpus benchmark falsified the first detector design, so the claim got smaller.

projects.name: kev-time
projects.description: CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue as a time series in plain SVG. A trend is legible before a report exists, and the page still loads on a phone during an incident.

projects.name: kelly-svg
projects.description: KEV entries grouped into effort clusters with exposure per cluster, so patch order follows effort and reach instead of catalogue order.

projects.name: Master's Thesis: Weather and Volatility
projects.description: A method for time cross-correlation of wind speed plus neural networks on long-term weather data, to quantify the volatility of solar and wind assets on the grid.
highlights: Developed a new method for temporal cross-correlation of wind-speed data with a gain above 70 percent in accuracy.
Trained neural networks on long-term weather data to optimise grid economics for intermittent solar and wind.

projects.name: Postgraduate Renewable Energy
projects.description: A postgraduate module on hydrogen production and storage, assessed with RETScreen for solar, wind, geothermal and biomass.
highlights: Analysed hydrogen production and storage projects with RETScreen.
Postgraduate research on renewables with a focus on solar, wind, geothermal and bioenergy.

projects.name: Vulnerability operations concept
projects.description: A sample vulnerability programme built from KEV data: exposure table, effort clusters, a 90-day method and a service model. Sample data throughout, and the page says so.
